content: Masterwort, scientifically known as Peucedanum ostruthium or Imperatoria ostruthium, belongs to the Apiaceae family. It should not be confused with great masterwort (Astrantia major), which is also part of the same botanical family. This plant typically thrives in woodland gardens and meadows, particularly in areas that are semi-shaded. The roots of masterwort, which are harvested during the spring or fall, are recognized for their numerous medicinal properties. These include tonic, antiseptic, emmenagogue (stimulating menstrual flow), and diuretic effects. The roots have been traditionally used to address issues such as flatulence, asthma, kidney stones, bladder stones, and water retention. Additionally, tea made from masterwort is believed to alleviate migraines and enhance the immune system.
